newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm on utility, refiner buying.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm on utility, refiner buying.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose slightly in range-bound and highly selective trade on Monday as an afternoon buying wave flared in shares of three private sector utilities and state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at 83,172.80, up 631 points, or 0.76 percent from Friday, after moving between 82,386 and 83,104. It had lost 1.5 percent last week.
Trade volume soared to 21.54 trillion lira ($217 million) from Friday's 14.95 trillion ($151.5 million) as hectic activity in the three utilities and Tupras made up 47 percent of the total turnover.
"Activity concentrated on the four stocks which have major impact both on the index and trade volume. Such highly selective movements are not healthy," said Turgay Ozaner from Global securities.
"I do not expect sharp (overall) movements in the stock market until uncertainty in other markets clears up," he added.

Turkish banks' dollar demand has recently been firm despite severe cash shortage and repeated central bank interventions. T-bill and bond yields have also been on an uptrend amid selling in the last two weeks.
